title: L0180
description: A compiled L0180 assessment item: the interaction a candidate sees, and the answer key that scores it. The two are siblings so a graded delivery can withhold `validation` and score on the server.

interaction.description: Everything the candidate sees. Safe to send to a browser.

validation.description: The answer key. Withheld when the item is delivered graded.

response.description: The candidate's response, attached by the delivery loop rather than the author. A list of option ids for a bare interaction; keyed by part id for a multi-part item.

choiceInteraction.title: Choice interaction
choiceInteraction.description: A stem and a list of options. Single-select unless maxChoices is above 1.

id.description: Present only when this interaction is a part of an item, where it keys the response.

cardinality.description: QTI cardinality, derived from maxChoices: one selection or several.

minChoices.description: Fewest options the candidate may select.

maxChoices.description: Most options the candidate may select. 1 is single-select.

shuffle.description: Present the options in random order.

options.description: The options offered, in authored order.

id.description: Identifier, derived as A, B, C… unless authored.

hottextInteraction.title: Hottext interaction
hottextInteraction.description: A passage cut into clickable units. Sentence granularity makes every sentence selectable; word granularity makes only the authored words selectable.

id.description: Present only when this interaction is a part of an item, where it keys the response.

granularity.description: What the units are: whole sentences, or single words.

within.description: Present when the units are the item's stimulus, which the renderer then shows in place of the static passage rather than twice.

units.description: The text in order. Everything is rendered; only `selectable` units can be clicked.

id.description: `p2.1` for the first sentence of paragraph 2; `w7` for the seventh word.

pre.description: Word granularity: punctuation before the clickable core, rendered outside it.

extendedTextInteraction.title: Extended-text interaction
extendedTextInteraction.description: A written response. Nothing scores it here — a person marks it against the rubric in `validation`, which is why its key is responseProcessing "human" rather than an unscored key.

id.description: Present only when this interaction is a part of an item, where it keys the response.

itemInteraction.title: Multi-part item
itemInteraction.description: An optional stimulus plus one or more interactions presented and scored together.

stimulus.description: The passage the parts are about.

paragraphs.description: One entry per paragraph, numbered for the reader so a stem can cite a line.

parts.description: The interactions, in presentation order. Each carries the id its response is keyed by.

responseValidation.title: Answer key for one interaction
responseValidation.description: The response-processing template decides the shape: map_response carries `mapping`, match_correct carries `correctResponse`. They are alternatives, never both.

responseProcessing.description: map_response scores each selected option and sums; match_correct awards the points for exactly the correct set and nothing otherwise.

points.description: The maximum achievable. Under map_response, the sum of the correct options only, so a penalty cannot move it.

mapping.description: map_response only: scoring per option id. Only scored options appear.

correct.description: Present and true when this option is a right answer.

points.description: What selecting this option is worth. Negative penalizes.

upperBound.description: map_response only: the most the mapping can earn. Below the sum of the correct entries it means "any N of them" — QTI's mapping@upper-bound.

correctResponse.description: match_correct only: the identifiers that must all be selected, and no others.

feedback.description: Why an option is wrong, keyed by option id. Shown only once that option is selected, so it never reveals an unpicked answer.

rubric.description: human only: the bands a person marks the response against, highest first.

descriptor.description: What a response has to do to earn it.

exemplar.description: human only: a response that would earn full marks.

points.description: What a fully correct response earns. Under conjunctive scoring this is the item's own points, not the sum of its parts.

scoring.description: additive sums the parts; conjunctive awards the points only when every part is fully correct.

parts.description: Per-part answer key, keyed by part id as the response is.
